consolidated_diary:
STRATEGIC BRIEFING FOR FUTURE DIPLOMACY GAMES

OPPONENT MODEL PROFILES

**google/gemma-4-31b-it (Austria this game):** Most reliable ally. Honored agreements roughly 70% of the time. Key pattern: they honor commitments that DIRECTLY benefit them (F AEG S BUL->CON worked because they gained Mediterranean access) but break support-only promises that don't gain them territory (broke A SER S BUL hold THREE consecutive turns). LESSON: Frame every request so their action gains them something. Never rely on their support for pure defense — always have a backup plan. They are genuinely alliance-oriented and won't stab unprovoked, but they're self-interested rather than selfless. Trust ceiling: 0.70. They make an excellent long-term ally if you align incentives correctly.

**deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (England this game):** EXTREME TURTLE. Held 3-5 units almost every single turn. Pattern: agrees to plans enthusiastically in messages, then holds units or executes different orders. Failed convoy in F1901 (promised NOR convoy, held everything). Failed A LON convoy in F1908 (agreed, held LON). Proposed physically impossible support orders (F BEL S F ENG->BRE — provinces not adjacent). LESSON: Never build strategy around deepseek executing agreed orders. They will passively benefit from YOUR actions while contributing nothing. They're useful only when their self-interest PERFECTLY aligns with your request AND requires minimal risk. Late-game they turned hostile when I grew large (attempted F NTH->NWG, called anti-Russia coalition). They are a natural late-game enemy because their passive fleet accumulation eventually makes them a threat. Best approach: use them as a shield early, plan to take their SCs in the endgame. Their passivity means their SCs are poorly defended once you commit forces.

**qwen/qwen3.5-27b (France this game):** Reliable mid-game ally who turns hostile when you grow dominant. Honored military support perfectly (A MUN S BER->KIE worked twice). Became openly hostile at 11 SCs, issued public anti-Russia coalition calls. Their coalition-building consistently FAILED because they acted too late. LESSON: Excellent early/mid-game coordination partner (0.80 trust for military execution). Plan to fight them in the late game regardless of early alliance. Their diplomatic influence is limited — other models didn't join their coalition calls. Militarily competent but not exceptional at defense (left MAR undefended in final turn because they prioritized punishing England over defending against me).

**qwen/qwen3.6-plus (Germany this game, eliminated):** DECEPTIVE BUT PREDICTABLE. Every message sounds perfect and reasonable ("verifiable compliance," "maintain eastern stability"). They broke the Baltic DMZ while swearing it was clear. However, their ACTUAL military play was mediocre — defended competently but never launched successful offensives. LESSON: Assume everything they say is false. Counter-intuitively, their deception makes them predictable: they will ALWAYS move into contested spaces while promising not to. Plan accordingly. They're dangerous early when you're exposed but collapse quickly under coordinated multi-front pressure (died in 1906 once France+England+Russia all attacked). Priority: eliminate them mid-game before they can build momentum.

**openai/gpt-5.4 (Italy this game):** Extremely defensive, fortress-mentality player. Built TRI to str 4 defense and held it the entire game. Will NOT commit to any diplomatic agreement without "board-proof" evidence. Refuses to negotiate on credit. LESSON: Don't waste diplomatic energy trying to recruit them for offensive campaigns. Instead, offer simple non-interference pacts with clear conditions (I gave them: "no moves involving AEG/ION/GRE/ALB/ADR/TRI"). They honor these pacts reliably (0.55 trust). Use them as a stable border you can ignore while fighting elsewhere. They won't stab you unless you directly threaten their corridor.

**grok-4.1-fast (Turkey this game, eliminated):** Aggressive and hostile from turn 1. Broke DMZ immediately (both went BLA in S1901). Will attack your home SCs even when diplomatic alternatives exist. LESSON: Never trust a DMZ with grok. Always go BLA in S1901 if playing Russia vs grok-Turkey. Their aggression is exploitable — they overcommit to attacks and leave defenses open (sent F BLA to attack SEV instead of defending RUM, losing RUM). Create forks that punish their aggression.

KEY STRATEGIC LESSONS

1. **ORDER SUBMISSION ERRORS ARE REAL:** My F STP/SC failed to move in S1901, and A SIL moved to BOH instead of supporting in F1905. Always mentally verify each order. Never assume complex orders submitted correctly.

2. **CHAIN MOVES ARE EXTREMELY RISKY:** A 5-unit chain where all depend on the lead unit succeeding will cascade-fail if the lead bounces. Only use chains when the lead move is guaranteed (into empty space) or you accept all units holding as the failure mode.

3. **FORK ATTACKS WIN GAMES:** The Turkey endgame (CON vs ANK fork) and the Germany zugzwang (KIE vs DEN) were decisive. When opponent can't defend both targets, you guarantee at least one capture.

4. **NEVER LEAVE HOME SCs UNDEFENDED:** Lost Sevastopol TWICE by pulling support away for offensive moves. Always maintain str 2 defense on vulnerable home centers.

5. **FRAME ALLIANCE REQUESTS AS MUTUAL GAINS:** gemma honored support when they gained territory, broke it when purely helping me. Always structure asks so allies gain something tangible.

6. **EARLY DMZ VIOLATIONS WIN TEMPO:** Going BLA in S1901 despite agreeing to DMZ is correct against aggressive opponents. The bounce costs nothing; success wins the game.
